question.problem:
Consider the linear transformation 
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3x+2y \\ -9x-6y\end{aligned}]$ 
and the vectors 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$
Which of the given vectors belong to the kernel of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

Therefore, we need to compute $T({v}_{i})$ for each vector ${v}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T({v}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\,T({v}_{1})=T({v}_{3})=0,$ we conclude that the only vectors that belong to the kernel of $\,T$ are $\,{v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}.$

choices.value: None of the given vectors belong to the kernel of $T$
